manifest.name: Go · net/http
manifest.description: Go standard library HTTP server (method routing since Go 1.22) with the pgx connection pool.
notes: GOMAXPROCS follows the container CPU limit automatically (Go 1.25+).

Each statement checks a connection out of the pgxpool (pool.QueryRow, pool.Exec), so /queries and /updates take one checkout per statement rather than one per request (idiomatic pgxpool usage without a transaction).
manifest.versions_note: Built from floating tags at run time; versions match the pinned ones closely but not exactly.

manifest.name: Java · Spring Boot
manifest.description: Spring Boot with Spring MVC on virtual threads, JdbcClient and HikariCP (16 connections), running on the Java 27 JVM.
notes: Virtual threads enabled (spring.threads.virtual.enabled).

Heap limited to 50 % of the container memory limit (-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=50, 512 MiB of 1 GiB) instead of the JDK default of 25 %, as production images usually do; default GC. Reported memory is bounded by this heap setting.

JdbcClient without a transaction checks a HikariCP connection out per statement, so /queries and /updates take one checkout per statement rather than one per request (idiomatic without a transaction).

manifest.name: TypeScript · Bun
manifest.description: Bun's built-in HTTP server and built-in PostgreSQL client (Bun.SQL), no dependencies.
notes: Two processes sharing the port via SO_REUSEPORT, each with an 8-connection pool.

/db and /list send their query through the shared Bun.sql pool. Bun's documentation suggests that it may pipeline queries of concurrent requests on one connection when prepared statements are enabled; this is the runtime's default behaviour and has not been verified by a packet capture.

manifest.name: Elixir · Plug + Bandit
manifest.description: Plug router on the Bandit HTTP server (the server Phoenix uses), Postgrex with prepared statements reused like Ecto does.
notes: Released with mix release; BEAM schedulers follow the container CPU limit.

Scheduler busy waiting disabled (+sbwt none +sbwtdcpu none +sbwtdio none in rel/vm.args.eex), the usual setting for CPU-limited containers, so idle schedulers do not spend the CPU quota while waiting for the database.

Postgrex pool of 16 connections with queue_target 5 s and queue_interval 10 s, so requests wait for a free connection like in the other stacks instead of being dropped by the DBConnection defaults (50 ms / 1 s).

startup.title: Cold start
startup.description: Starts a fresh container several times and measures the time until GET /json first succeeds. Also records memory at idle and the image size.

cold.title: Cold load
cold.description: GET /db at full load for 10 seconds right after start, without any warm-up. Shows how much a runtime needs to warm up (JIT, caches, pools) after scaling out.

json.title: JSON
json.description: GET /json returns a small JSON object. Pure framework and serialization overhead, no I/O.

db.title: Single query
db.description: GET /db reads one random row by primary key and returns it as JSON.

queries.title: 20 queries
queries.description: GET /queries runs 20 sequential primary-key reads on one connection and returns them as a JSON array. Measures driver and async efficiency.

updates.title: Updates
updates.description: GET /updates reads 5 random rows, changes each value and writes it back with 5 UPDATE statements.

list.title: List
list.description: GET /list reads a range of 100 rows, adds a computed field to each and serializes the list, like a typical paginated REST endpoint.

orders.title: JSON POST
orders.description: POST /orders sends a 2.5 KB order with 50 line items. The service parses, validates and totals it and returns a summary. No database.

db-c16.title: Single query, 16 connections
db-c16.description: GET /db with only 16 concurrent connections: behaviour at moderate concurrency, where latency rather than queueing dominates.

db-c512.title: Single query, 512 connections
db-c512.description: GET /db with 512 concurrent connections: many idle keep-alive connections and deep queues on 2 cores.

rate.title: Fixed load (5,000 req/s)
rate.description: GET /db at a fixed 5,000 requests per second for every implementation (open loop, latency corrected for coordinated omission). Shows latency at normal production load instead of at saturation.
